findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars, so cache status stays on screen
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` onSuccess only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()` (which is the parent's optional `onChanged`). It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the sibling `disconnectMutation` which calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`. After a successful cache deletion, if `onChanged` does not itself refetch the query (in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` it is just `props.onChanged`), the dropdown/first render keeps showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` and the 'Delete cached data' action, even though the cache is gone. Add invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the deleteCache mutation's onSettled.

findings.title: Delegation-credential users can see Delete cache but the handler rejects them
findings.body: The handler authorizes by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. For a delegation credential the underlying `Credential` row is owned by the admin/organization, not the delegate user, so a delegate user who has cache data will get 'Credential not found or access denied'. Meanwhile `CredentialActionsDropdown` renders the 'Delete cached data' item purely on `hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` (it does not exclude `delegationCredentialId` the way `canDisconnect` does), so the button is shown to delegate users and fails with an error toast. Either exclude delegation credentials from the delete-cache UI, or authorize deletion using the delegation path / userId-based cache ownership.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId with empty data is a redundant write that may not bump updatedAt
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` intending to refresh `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Passing an empty `data` object is a no-op for the columns; Prisma's `@updatedAt` is not reliably applied when there are no fields to change, so the intended timestamp refresh likely does not happen. Furthermore, nothing reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for this feature (the PR states the frontend uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so this is an unnecessary extra DB write on the hot cache-population/webhook path for every credential. Remove it (or pass explicit data and surface it in the UI if it is actually needed).

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiry, so expired cache is reported as present
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates `_max(updatedAt)` over all `CalendarCache` rows for the credential without filtering on `expiresAt`. Cache entries past `expiresAt` are never served by `getCachedAvailability`, but the UI will still show 'Cache Status' / 'Last updated' and offer to delete it, implying a usable cache exists. Consider adding `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` if 'has cache' should mean 'has servable cache'.

findings.title: Widening the exported UserWithCalendars input type to require updatedAt/googleChannelId risks compile breaks
findings.body: The exported `UserWithCalendars` type now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on both `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`, yet nothing in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` consumes these fields for this feature. Only the `findUnlockedUserForSession` producer in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts` was updated. Any other caller that builds this input without selecting those columns (e.g. the `@calcom/platform-libraries` re-export of this function, or other query sites feeding `allSelectedCalendars`) will now fail type-check. If these fields are not actually used, drop the type change; otherwise update every producer/select.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only; script silently misbehaves on Linux
findings.body: The in-place edit uses BSD sed syntax `sed -i '' -E ...`. On GNU sed (Linux CI/devcontainers) `-i ''` is parsed differently, so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL line is not replaced as intended. Given this is a committed dev/test helper, use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and move) or detect the platform.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` ignores the user's locale. Cal.com users in other locales will see US-style dates in the 'Last updated' string even though the rest of the UI is localized via `useLocale`. Format using the active locale (or pass no locales to `Intl.DateTimeFormat` so the runtime default is used).
